aspects.says: DE 55 is a list of BER-TLV objects: a tag that continues while its bytes say so, a length in one byte or after 81 or 82, and exactly that many value bytes.
basis: section:3.6. DE 55 Is a List of Tag-Length-Value Objects, Read as Bytes

aspects.says: ISO 8583:2023 builds some fields from datasets, which jPOS 2.1.7 reads only as opaque binary.
basis: section:3.6. DE 55 Is a List of Tag-Length-Value Objects, Read as Bytes
aspects.reason: a pointer to units 17 and s13; jPOS 2.1.7 offers nothing to practise on this edition

aspects.says: Through the stock ASCII packager DE 55 comes back as text, so it is read with getBytes, never parsed from getString.
basis: section:3.6. DE 55 Is a List of Tag-Length-Value Objects, Read as Bytes
aspects.reason: the difference shows only between a built and a received message through one stock packager; the page runs it, and read-chip-data already works on the bytes

aspects.says: One field written in another format shifts every field after it, so the receiver's error names a later field that is correct.
basis: section:3.1. A Field's Format Is All the Receiver Has to Find Where It Ends

aspects.says: Nothing in the bytes marks where a field ends: a fixed field takes its width and a variable one its length prefix, two digits for LLVAR and three for LLLVAR.
basis: section:3.1. A Field's Format Is All the Receiver Has to Find Where It Ends

aspects.says: Which fields must be present is set per MTI by the network's specification; there is no list that holds for every message.
basis: section:3.5. Which Fields Must Be Present Depends on the MTI and the Network

aspects.says: jPOS checks a value's length and nothing else, so a dot or a letter in a numeric field goes to the host.
basis: section:3.2. A Short Value Is Padded, a Long One Is Refused, and Nothing Else Is Checked

aspects.says: ASCII, BCD and EBCDIC packagers write the same field differently, and a BCD length prefix counts digits, not bytes.
basis: section:3.3. The Packager Decides the Bytes, So Both Peers Need the Same One

aspects.says: A short fixed value is padded (numbers with zeros on the left, text with spaces on the right) and a value that is too long is refused, never cut.
basis: section:3.2. A Short Value Is Padded, a Long One Is Refused, and Nothing Else Is Checked

aspects.says: Track 2 is set with = in the ISOMsg; a BCD packager packs a D character as the digit 4 and the separator is lost.
basis: section:3.4. A Field's Type Decides How You Read Its Value

aspects.says: Amounts are parsed as a long of minor units, DE 7 is read with ISODate, and binary fields are byte arrays read with getBytes.
basis: section:3.4. A Field's Type Decides How You Read Its Value
aspects.reason: these are single library calls with no rule of their own that a test could grade beyond calling the method
